1.explanation: All of the broken ARIA attributes and naming are coming from the React Dropdown component’s render method. In render(), getButtonProps is used to wire up the trigger <ListBox.Field>, which ends up emitting invalid aria-owns/aria-controls (because the menu id generated in <ListBox.Menu> does not match) and an aria-label that does not include the visible label text. Additionally, the menu is never wired up with Downshift’s getMenuProps, so the id handed to the menu and the id referenced by the button become out of sync. Fixing this requires updating render(): • spread getMenuProps onto <ListBox.Menu> and ensure its id matches the one used by getButtonProps, • adjust the aria-label passed to the button (via getButtonProps or translateWithId) so it includes the visible label text, and • align the menu id naming to be a valid value for aria-owns/aria-controls.
1.bug_scenario: When using the React version of the Carbon Dropdown component with VoiceOver (and other accessibility tooling), two accessibility violations are reported: 1) “ARIA attributes must conform to valid values,” specifically aria-owns and aria-controls pointing at an invalid or mismatched menu id; and 2) “Accessible name does not contain the visible label text,” because the button’s accessible name (e.g. “open menu”) doesn’t include the dropdown’s visible label (e.g. “Dropdown menu options”). The screenshots show the inspector highlighting a <div role="button"> with aria-haspopup, aria-expanded, aria-owns and aria-controls set to a generated id (carbon-dropdown-example__menu) that doesn’t match a valid ID on the menu, and whose aria-label (“open menu”) fails to reference the visible text.

2.explanation: The Accessibility violations stem from the render() method in Dropdown.js. In that function the component uses Downshift’s getButtonProps on ListBox.Field to render a <div role="button" …>, passing through aria-controls/aria-owns (pointing at the menu id built as `${id}__menu`) and an aria-label that doesn’t reflect the visible text. Because the generated ID (‘carbon-dropdown-example__menu’) doesn’t conform to ARIA identifier syntax, and the aria-label fails to include the actual label, the accessibility rules are broken. Fixing this requires editing the render() logic in Dropdown.js to generate a compliant ID and to compute an accessible name that includes the visible label text.
2.bug_scenario: When the React-based Carbon Dropdown is rendered, the trigger element (<div role="button">) is injected with invalid ARIA attributes (aria-owns and aria-controls point at an ID containing double underscores), and its aria-label (“open menu”) does not include the visible label text (“Dropdown menu options”), causing two DAP violations: “ARIA attributes must conform to valid values” and “Accessible name does not contain the visible label text.”
